item.title: Asuka-nabe: The Ancient Milk Hot Pot of Asuka — Guide
item.description: Asuka-nabe is one of Japan’s most unusual regional hot pots: a chicken-and-vegetable nabe simmered in a broth enriched with milk, giving it a mellow, creamy character unlike any other Japanese pot. Its origins are traced to the Asuka period over 1,300 years ago, when dairy foods and cattle-keeping were introduced to Japan from the Asian mainland via the imperial court based in Asuka — making this humble dish a living echo of Japan’s very first encounter with milk.
